verdict.tagline: Swings that tire your arms and a community that tests your patience.
for_you_if: you want a genuinely physical workout from your games
you can master momentum-based movement over time
you enjoy fast-paced tag mechanics in virtual reality
not_for_you_if: you need stable connection setups through Steam VR
you want to avoid disruptive voice chat behavior
you object to paying for the PC version

This game is okay, but it gets boring pretty quickly. Don’t get me wrong, I do like it, but the “infection” gamemode starts to feel repetitive after like 2 - 5 rounds. The other “super” gamemodes also make it less fun sometimes since players can use stuff like long arms and other gadgets that kind of change the balance.

Casual mode is alright and probably the best way to meet people, but it’s often filled with little kids screaming, which makes it kinda annoying to be in one. 

The anti cheat is kinda annoying if your trying to mod in this game though, even if your alone in a private.

Overall I’d give it a 7.2/10. But $20 doesn’t really feel worth it for what you get, but it should probably be closer to $10–$15.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Movement grows intuitive past the initial learning curve and moderation tools help manage disruptive players.

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering mean or toxic players, noting that voice chat can be turned off or players can be muted and reported on the leaderboard.

citations.review_text: its just a fun game in general but there is alot of mean people in the game

Gorilla tag is really good for making friends and having fun, but there are some players who will try to make you feel unwelcome. If you run into that sort of player report them on the leaderboard. As in the game itself though, it is really entertaining and even has different gamemodes. You can play minigames with others or play tag, you can even play a gamemode which has you look for certain players and tag them. Overall the game has endless possibilities and theres no limit to your experience with it.
